statement: The hexagonal SAW connective constant is sqrt(2+sqrt(2)); the sqrt(1+sqrt(2)) value printed just before Grimmett Question 2.2 is inconsistent with the cited theorem.
assumptions: Hexagonal lattice; connective constant defined by n-step growth
source: https://www.unige.ch/~smirnov/papers/saw-j.pdf, Theorem 1, printed p.1654; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.07318, printed p.3
source_quote: For the hexagonal lattice, μ = sqrt(2 + sqrt(2))
proof_or_counterexample: Source-fidelity comparison of Duminil-Copin–Smirnov Theorem 1 with Grimmett's displayed formula; not an independent proof of the theorem.
remaining_gap: Confirm printed source typography; do not infer P0003 solved from connective constant.

statement: For a finite collection of vertex-simple paths weighted by x^length with x>0, conditioning on a feasible length n yields the uniform law over n-step paths in that same collection; a specified endpoint and domain remain constraints, and convergence of the unconditioned law does not alone determine the selected-length law.
source_quote: Every path surviving the condition has weight x^n
proof_or_counterexample: Cancel common x^n within the selected-length collection; w400's rare atom example has identical weak joint limits but opposite conditional shape laws at the selected length.
independent_reviewer: w401 independent mathematical check of w400 claims
remaining_gap: No quantitative relative local limit or endpoint/domain transfer for the actual honeycomb SAW has been proved.

statement: For abstract nonnegative sequences c_n=1 and a_n=1+epsilon*(-1)^n, 0<epsilon<1, the real critical generating-function ratio A(z)/C(z) tends to 1 as z tends to 1 from below, but the coefficient ratios a_n/c_n do not converge.
assumptions: real z tends to 1 from below
proof_or_counterexample: C(z)=1/(1-z) and A(z)=1/(1-z)+epsilon/(1+z). The quotient is 1+epsilon*(1-z)/(1+z)->1, while a_n/c_n=1+epsilon*(-1)^n oscillates.
remaining_gap: Independent audit by w404; this abstract diagnostic gives no SAW coefficient asymptotic or scaling limit.
